guide: Shows a travel app's demo account and its "Wrapped" feature: a Spotify-style recap of every trip you have taken. You need an AI coding assistant (ChatGPT Codex or Claude Code), a database such as Supabase, and a host such as Vercel.
1. Describe the app in one paragraph to Claude Code or Codex: who it is for, and the single feature you want to show first.
1. Create a Supabase project and add tables for users, trips (place, country, start date, end date) and the order of stops.
1. Build the recap view: group a user's trips by year and by all time, and list the stops in order, for example Paris, Santorini, Reykjavik, Tokyo.
1. Add a demo account with made-up trips, so anyone can try the app without signing up or sharing their own data.
1. Add a clear "Demo" label and make the demo account read-only, so visitors cannot change or delete the sample data.
1. Deploy the app to Vercel and test the demo login from a phone and a laptop.
1. Screen-record a walkthrough of the recap and post it, saying plainly that it is a demo account.
Watch out: use invented trips and a throwaway email for the demo account, never a real person's travel history, and lock the demo to read-only so visitors cannot break it.

```
You are helping me build a travel app with a "Wrapped" style recap, similar to a Spotify year-in-review but for trips. I use <Claude Code or Codex>, Supabase for the database and login, and Vercel for hosting. My app is called <app name> and is for <audience>.
Build this:
1. A database schema in Supabase with users, trips (place, country, start date, end date) and ordered stops.
2. A recap page that shows a user's trips for a chosen year and for all time, with the stops listed in order.
3. A demo account filled with invented trips, such as <city 1>, <city 2> and <city 3>. It must be read-only, clearly labelled "Demo", and use Supabase row-level security so visitors cannot edit or delete data.
4. A "Try the demo" button on the home page that logs visitors straight into the demo account.
Constraints: use no real personal data, keep secrets in environment variables and out of the code, and make the pages work well on a phone.
Return the full file list, the SQL for the tables and security rules, the code for each file, and step-by-step instructions to deploy on Vercel.
```
Skipped: no checks against a live app; the steps are inferred from the transcript, which describes only the demo and Wrapped view.
